title: Mined public X pairs with a one-word delta, grouped stored-leaf birthday search

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold algorithm of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 over the challenge and fresh coins: one fresh 64-bit coin opens the run with probability K/2^64, K = 7195457751245803577, the least integer with (K/2^64) lo_run >= 0.39, lo_run the exact opened-run bound of success.md 6.5 (every abort, drop, cap, defect and the fixup meter charged as failure rows). Its expected total work is at most 2^123.309256957682979 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit), (2^7 + (K/2^64) E_run)/1000 with E_run in instructions; E_run over all planned leaves is at most 57.2029 instructions per planned leaf (success.md 6.6); the worst case, < 2^190.602588 instructions, is disclosed. The run first mines 2^14 pairs of public points [s]P whose y^2 differ by less than 2^63 (Phase 0, charged, capped; aborts with no padding branch on proof.md 2.3's tests), then runs proof.md's grouped stored-leaf birthday search with those X's. Peak memory at most 2^135.8120 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^115.9395 units, Phase 0 included; no advice; certificate.py checks every declared figure. No prior acceptance or score is a premise. An analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Kernels, sites, fixups, labels, ygen and both hops (8 generators, 16 homes) against bit-exact models; Phase 0; the resolver; every kernel count against certificate.py, which it runs (proof.md 8). Not a production-scale attack.
